why:
I checked both must_catch items, and the briefs handle both.

Item 1: The builder brief names "test/csv.test.js uses node:test and execFileSync to run the CLI" in its current state, then says "Keep the existing tests passing". It also requires the CSV behaviour to keep working, both as a pre-PR check and as an acceptance line: `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` -> `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]`. It tells the builder to leave src/parse.js alone ("The simplest change is to src/parse.js not at all", which is garbled but clear enough) and to call parse(text) "exactly as now" without the flag. So the CSV path is protected. One weakness: it never says outright that parse() is shared with the CSV path.

Item 2: Verifier check 6 runs "npm test; echo \"exit=$?\"". The advisory says "there is no such script" for `npm run test:cli` and to use npm test instead.
